title: Bunny OS service capability manifest
description: What one Bunny OS service or feature declares it needs. Implementations are the degradation ladder: rank 1 is the richest form and higher ranks are progressively reduced, so implementation selection and degradation are the same deterministic walk and cannot disagree. A manifest declares requirements only; it never declares an outcome, a mode, or a hardware class. There is no field in which a product tier could be written.

minimumBytes.description: Below this the service cannot start. Checked against the allocatable budget, never against free physical memory.

recommendedBytes.description: Granted instead of the minimum when the budget can afford it, so a service is not left permanently reclaiming.

minimumCores.description: Effective cores, which include any cgroup quota.

runtime.description: 'any' means a bound driver and a render node. A named runtime must have been verified; the presence of a PCI device never satisfies this.

minimumVramBytes.description: Compared against the largest single device, never the sum: work must fit in one of them.

scores.description: Gates on named capability dimensions, so a service can require e.g. storage_performance >= 40 without a bespoke field being invented for it.

essential.description: An essential service is part of the control plane. It is funded off the top before any discretionary pool exists, must have a local implementation, and may only depend on other essential services.

priority.description: Importance under contention, as a band name or 0..100. This is a ranking among services within one Bunny OS, not a product tier. The band names deliberately avoid 'low' and 'high': in this codebase those are reserved words, and a manifest containing them should be a validation failure rather than something a reader has to disambiguate.

budgetCategory.description: Must be 'essential_services' if and only if essential is true. Essential memory is taken off the top rather than competed for; a category that could be outbid would not be essential.

handlesSensitiveData.description: When true, no remote implementation may be selected unless remoteExecution.allowSensitiveData is explicitly true, independently of whether remote execution is enabled at all.

conflictsWith.description: Must be declared symmetrically by both services, or the engine's decision would depend on evaluation order.

rank.description: 1 is the richest implementation. The engine takes the first whose requirements are met, walking upward.

provider.description: Required in practice for remote implementations: an unnamed destination cannot be allowlisted, so it can never be authorised.

sendsUserDataRemotely.description: May not be false when locality is 'remote'.
